summary.oneLiner: The company has scaled revenue 7-10x in 1.5 years via acquisition of an established biscuit brand and aggressive export expansion through contract manufacturing, with a new 5,000 MT plant in UP set to commission by Oct 2026, doubling capacity and shifting mix toward higher-margin premium products.

one-line thesis: The company has scaled revenue 7-10x in 1.5 years via acquisition of an established biscuit brand and aggressive export expansion through contract manufacturing, with a new 5,000 MT plant in UP set to commission by Oct 2026, doubling capacity and shifting mix toward higher-margin premium products.
financial scorecard: Revenue: +500% YoY (Rs. 526cr 9M FY25 → guided Rs. 700cr FY25); EBITDA/margin: ~9% (low due to high contract manufacturing mix); PAT (rptd): Not disclosed; PAT (normalized): Implied strong growth from premium segment; Order book: Not disclosed; Net debt: Zero debt, cash equivalents Rs. 60 lakh
guidance: Revenue growth: 50% YoY in FY26 (to Rs. 1,000cr), 70-75% in FY27 (to Rs. 1,200cr); Margin: EBITDA to improve to 15-17% post new plant; Order inflow: Strong export demand from Middle East, Africa, South America; Capex/commissioning: Rs. 400-500cr for new plant, COD Oct 2026
order book & pipeline: Not disclosed; export orders from consolidators in Middle East/Africa/South America; contract manufacturing pipeline active
segment / subsidiary detail: Domestic (Nurture Well Foods): Rs. 425cr biscuits (80-85% of Rs. 526cr 9M), 75% India, 25% export; Dubai subsidiary (Nurture Well LLC): Rs. 350cr contract manufacturing (100% export); Contract manufacturing: ~10-12% of Indian ops, 100% of Dubai ops
growth verticals / optionality: Expansion into Eastern/Western India distribution; entry into wafer cones, chocolates, probiotic cookies; potential to shift Dubai contract manufacturing to new UP plant; targeting Indian diaspora in US/Europe
margins & cost dynamics: Gross margin: 15-20% (industry standard); Contract manufacturing margin: 12-13% (protected by 3-4 day raw material lock-in); Premium products in new plant expected to lift EBITDA to 15-17%
capex / expansion: Rs. 400-500cr for new 5,000 MT plant in Uttar Pradesh; land acquired, DPR under finalization; funding mix: equity, debt, internal accruals
capital allocation: Funds raised via India Inflection Opportunities Fund used for working capital and growth; new capex to be funded via mix of equity, debt, and accruals; no dividend policy mentioned
risks & watch-items: Raw material price volatility (mitigated by 3-4 day lock-in); reliance on contract manufacturing partners in Malaysia/Indonesia; execution risk in new plant commissioning; competition from Britannia/Parle; currency risk in exports
management quality / tone: Highly confident, aggressive, and execution-focused; clear roadmap for growth; transparent on capex and funding plans; emphasis on distribution strength and premium product shift
non-obvious takeaways: Dubai subsidiary's Rs. 350cr revenue is contract manufacturing, not trading — it's a high-volume, low-margin but cash-efficient engine that funds domestic expansion; the 75% domestic sales figure is only for the Indian subsidiary, not consolidated
